fatal_errors: No specific surface-modification method is identified; the target used atmospheric plasma spraying of an AlCoCrFeNi high-entropy-alloy coating followed by annealing.
The critical optimum treatment of 550 °C for 2 h is omitted.
The proposed mechanism merely restates that surface properties are improved and does not identify grain refinement, sluggish diffusion, or formation of Al- and Cr-rich passive oxides.
No quantitative or cited evidence supports the corrosion-resistance claim.
The broad claim across unspecified challenging environments exceeds the demonstrated boundaries and omits that the source article was retracted.
explanation: The hypothesis recognizes the general problem and predicts that surface modification could improve stainless-steel corrosion resistance, but it largely repeats the prompt rather than answering which method should be used and why. It does not reconstruct the APS-deposited AlCoCrFeNi coating, the 550 °C annealing condition, the relevant passive-layer mechanism, or the sulfuric-acid and molten-salt test environments. Its modified-versus-unmodified control is directionally appropriate, but the proposed measurements and environment are too vague to discriminate the target treatment from other surface modifications. With no evidence and an overbroad boundary, it is unsupported rather than a meaningful reconstruction.
